findings.title: The red check can still hide a relay-only browser check behind a failing direct run
findings.why: bothSuites runs `npm run test:browsers`, and package.json defines that as `node tests/two-browser.mjs && node tests/two-browser.mjs --relay`. If an earlier test: commit adds a browser check that fails in the direct run (its fix comes later), the relay run never starts. A later test: commit whose new check only fails under --relay then gets the same wrong stop this PR is meant to fix: 'no assertion fails in one of its new tests'. The fix moves the short-circuit one level down without removing it. The two two-browser runs should each run, with their exit codes combined, like the unit and browser suites are now.

findings.title: The new test only checks the source text, not what the command does
findings.why: The test regex-matches the literal strings `npmTest(dir, { bothSuites: true })` and `test:unit; u=$?; npm run test:browsers; b=$?`. It never checks that the shell command keeps running after a failure or exits non-zero when only one suite fails. A rewording that works the same way would fail the test, and a broken command with the same substrings (for example a wrong exit expression) would pass it. That is also why it missed the `&&` still inside test:browsers.
